observation_summary: The 'add' method in BasicMonthOfYearDateTimeField attempts to convert a partial date into a full instant using a default year (1970), which is not a leap year. This causes an IllegalFieldValueException when the partial contains February 29th, as the validation logic rejects the 29th in a non-leap year.
hypothesis: The 'add' method in BasicMonthOfYearDateTimeField incorrectly attempts to convert a partial date (like MonthDay) into a full instant by setting it on a default epoch (1970-01-01). Since 1970 is not a leap year, setting the day-of-month to 29 for February causes an IllegalFieldValueException. The logic fails to account for the fact that MonthDay is year-agnostic and should handle month arithmetic without forcing a specific year context that might invalidate the day.
prediction: The fix will involve bypassing the full-instant conversion logic for MonthDay objects (or similar contiguous partials where the month is the largest field) and performing the month arithmetic directly on the partial's values.
